newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-DRAVID LIFTS INDIA WITH MAIDEN TEST CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DRAVID LIFTS INDIA WITH MAIDEN TEST CENTURY.

text.p: Rahul Dravid defied South Africa for nine hours while compiling his maiden test century to carry India to 410 all out on the second day of the third and final test at the Wanderers on Friday.
Playing his ninth test, Dravid came in at the fall of the first wicket at 25 on Thursday and was last out after scoring 148 from 362 balls with 21 boundaries.
In reply, South Africa's opening pair of Andrew Hudson and Gary Kirsten faced just two balls before bad light ended play 12.4 overs early with the home side nought for no wicket.
Heavy overnight rain prevented play until after lunch and when India resumed at 233 for three, Dravid lost his overnight partner in the sixth over of the day.

Saurav Ganguly added five to his score before edging Lance Klusener to Brian McMillan at second slip, having made 73 came from 138 balls with 13 fours and a six. He added 145 for the fourth wicket with Dravid.

Mohammad Azharuddin produced a brief, sparkling cameo of 18 in 20 balls before Venkat Laxman became Klusener's third victim in a hostile spell when he was forced to retire hurt to the fourth ball he faced.
Struck on the hand by a short delivery from Klusener, Laxman had the little finger of his left hand broken and will take no further part in the match. He will be out of the game for three weeks.
India were effectively 266 for six, but lower order defiance from Anil Kumble and Javagal Srinath ensured support for Dravid's monumental innings.
Kumble made 29 out of a seventh wicket stand worth 61 and Srinath hit merrily for 41 in an eighth wicket partnership of 76 before skying Donald to mid-wicket.
Donald then disposed of Doda Ganesh for a single and South African captain Hansie Cronje got the prize scalp of Dravid caught at mid-off to round off the innings.
With few signs of deterioration in the Wanderers pitch, the match seems likely to be a draw.
South Africa have a 2-0 winning lead in the series.
